DUME Bien que son utilisation ne soit pas obligatoire, l’Ined encourage fortement les candidats à renseigner un Document Unique de Marché Européen (DUME) pour candidater. 1.1. Qu’est-ce que le DUME Le DUME est un formulaire électronique standardisé qui permet à un opérateur économique de présenter sa candidature à un marché public en déclarant son identité, sa situation juridique, financière et ses capacités professionnelles. Il est accessible en ligne, notamment via la plateforme https://dume.chorus -pro.gouv.fr ou directement depuis certains profils acheteurs sur https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr. Grâce à ce formulaire, l’entreprise peut bénéficier d’un pré remplissage automatique de certaines informations à partir de son numéro SIRET, ce qui réduit le nombre de saisies. Un même opérateur économique ne peut se présenter pour un même marché public en agissant à la fois en qualité de candidat individuel et de membre d’un ou plusieurs groupements, ni en qualité de membre de plusieurs groupements. Au sein de la présente consultation, il n'est exigé aucune forme de groupement pa rticulier ou de solidarité du mandataire. Contrôle qualité et conformité Le Titulaire met en œuvre des procédures internes de contrôle qualité permettant d'assurer la conformité des prestations aux caractéristiques de la commande et au BAT validé par l'Ined. Pour les impressions en quadrichromie et lorsque la nature de la prestation le justifie, le titulaire assure la maîtrise de son procédé d'impression conformément aux référentiels de la série ISO 12647 ou équivalent, notamment en matière de contrôle colorimétrique. Avant chaque livraison, le Titulaire ef fectue un contrôle de conformité portant notamment sur le support, le format, le grammage, les couleurs, le nombre d'exemplaires, le façonnage et le conditionnement. Le Titulaire signale immédiatement à l'Ined toute anomalie constatée. Les produits présent ant un défaut ou une non -conformité sont remplacés à ses frais lorsqu'ils ne sont pas conformes aux caractéristiques de la commande ou au BAT validé. Le Titulaire s’engage à réaliser tous les types de façonnage listés dans le bordereau des prix et précisés dans chaque commande.

L’Ined, en qualité de responsable du traitement, détermine les finalités et les moyens du traitement et transmet au Titulaire les données nécessaires à l’exécution des prestations. Le Titulaire, en qualité de sous-traitant au sens de la réglementation applicable à la protection des données à caractère personnel, traite les données uniquement pour les besoins de l’exécution du marché et conformément aux instructions de l’Ined. Les parties s’engagent à respecter les obligations qui leur incombent en matière de protection des données à caractère personnel, conformément à l’Annexe 2. Enclosed please find the Request for Quotation (RFQ) package, including the proposed technical specifications, for the Procurement of Printing Services for the U.S. Embassy in Hanoi, covering the period November 2026 to December 2030. If you would like to submit a quotation, please complete the required portions of the attached document and submit it to the address indicated on the Standard Form 18 included with this letter. Your submission must include the following: - Standard Form 18: Complete blocks 11e & 11f (Price), and blocks 13, 14, 15 and 16 (Bidder’s information) - Pricing: As per RFQ Section C - Technical Proposal: As required in RFQ - NDAA certification Your quotation must be submitted electronically to HanoiGSOProcurement

7:00 local time. Quotations received after this deadline will not be accepted. All quotations must be submitted in English; incomplete proposals will not be considered. Any questions regarding this RFQ please submit HanoiGSOProcurement@state.gov on or before October 12, 2026 at 17:00 local time. Questions submitted after this deadline will not be answered. Answers from the Embassy will be issued no later than October 15, 2026 local time. The U.S. Government intends to establish the Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with the responsible offerors submitting the lowest-priced, technically acceptable quotation that meets all solicitation requirements. The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate issue experience. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. The scope covers four primary initial accession pipelines: (1) Initial Entry Training (IET) Soldiers processing through Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS); (2) United States Military Academy (West Point) Cadets; (3) contracted Senior Reserve Officers' Training Co

Their strategic focus centers on logistics modernization through integrated information systems, scaling artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) analytics, and improving supply chain reliability across Army operations. The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate iss

l, non- contact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is seeking a solution that will operate reliably across a wide spectrum of Army operating environments, minimize the training burden on Soldiers and administering staff, and be capable of integrating with designated Army data systems to support downstream sizing and issue processes. 3. REQUIRED AND DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES. Required Attributes: The proposed solution shall meet the following mandatory requirements: • Comprehensive Scanning and Environmental Resilience: Must capture both body and foot measurements sufficient to determine standard Army uniform and footwear sizing using automated, digital, non-contact methods that eliminate manual measurements. The capture hardware must be transportable and capable of operating reliably across a wide spectrum of environments, including indoor facilities and austere outdoor settings, accommodating real-world conditions such as variable ambient lighting and physical space constraints. • Data Translation & Mapping: Must translate captured body and foot measurements into recommen

tive, requiring minimal training for both the Soldiers and Cadets being measured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). Impact Level 5 (IL5) is required prior to full-scale enterprise deployment. Pilot execution will be conducted in an isolated, test/dummy network environment. • Data Management & Privacy: Must support a defined data retention and deletion schedule that strictly adheres to Army records-management and Privacy Act requirements. • Inclusive Accuracy: Must produce accurate measurements across the complete spectrum of body types, statures, and physical compositions represented in the Army accession and training population. • Accessibility (Section 508): Must provide an accessible alternative process for Soldiers and Cadets who are unable to use, or elect not to use, the scanning solution; any user-facing digital interface must strictly comply with Section 508 accessibility standards. • Data Ownership & Licensing: Must allow the Government to retain exclusive ownership of all Soldier and Cadet sizing data as well as any vendor-generated technical or derived data. • Hardware Agility & Openness: The proposed solution must be hardware-

insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit
